title: Skybridge x Redwood - Marketplace integration & reference arch sync
summary: Technical sync to align on Redwood marketplace listing requirements, joint reference architecture for private deployments in Skybridge marketplace, and next steps for integration QA and launch timeline.
next_steps: Redwood to share marketplace listing template and required assets (logo, screenshots, description) by 2026-06-18
Skybridge to provide VPC peering/contact for networking tests and preferred regions by 2026-06-20
SE team to run initial perf baseline on Skybridge staging (quantized model) and share results by 2026-06-25
Schedule follow-up runbook review and legal checklist handoff week of 2026-06-29
action_items: Ava Chen: Share marketplace listing template + example listing; due 2026-06-18
Marcus Patel: Prepare initial perf test plan and quantization recommendations; due 2026-06-22
Sofia Martinez: Provide Skybridge staging VPC details and IAM contacts; due 2026-06-20
Noah Kim: Compile reference arch notes for on-prem variants; due 2026-06-24
Priya Rao: Draft joint go-to-market brief for internal review; due 2026-06-28
transcript: 00:00:00 - Ava Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes today. quick intro from redwood side?

00:00:08 - Liam O'Connor: yep thanks ava, liam here from skybridge
ash i'll quick share context, we're launching a marketplace push in q3 and want redwood listed as our managed inference partner
00:00:22 - Marcus Patel: great, Marcus from SE. i'll focus on the reference arch and perf expectations. not to over promise but we want to make sure the private deployment story is smooth
00:00:34 - Sofia Martinez: hi, so i'm the marketplace engineer, i'll handle the listing onboarding and asset requirements, and coordinate the validation pipeline
00:00:46 - Ava Chen: perfect. agenda: listing fields, ref arch for vpc/on-prem, joint solution packaging/pricing, tests, and security checklist. any other items?
00:00:58 - Noah Kim: one ask — we want a short runbook for rollback and fallback model variants in case of capacity issues, customers care about graceful degradation
00:01:08 - Priya Rao: noted. we'll include fallback guidance — redwood has model variant routing but we'll explain in marketplace docs
00:01:20 - Liam O'Connor: sounds good. so starting with the listing — what metadata do you need?

00:01:28 - Marcus Patel: we typically need short & long descriptions, feature bullets (streaming, function calls, embeddings), supported models and perf profiles, pricing tier recommendations, screenshots, logos, and a one-page reference arch PDF
00:01:44 - Sofia Martinez: okay can you send an example with recommended image dimensions and a marketing blurb? sometimes the automated validator flags text length or unsupported chars

00:01:54 - Ava Chen: yes we'll send the template. note: sometimes redwood model names get transcribed oddly in docs — e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' might show up as 'redwood dedicate' in earlier assets — we'll make sure canonical names are clear

00:02:10 - Noah Kim: on reference arch: our customers may run in two flavors — managed marketplace-hosted (Redwood hosted) and private (VPC or on-prem). for private we need network diagrams, peering steps, kms guidance

00:02:24 - Marcus Patel: agreed. for private deployments we recommend a reference arch with three zones: control plane (redwood control, optional managed), inference pool (gpu nodes), and customer data plane (s3 or object store). we'll include example terraform snippets — though snippet may need customizing per cloud
00:02:40 - Sofia Martinez: terraform snippets are great; our validator requires a small sample deploy script for the listing — can be sanitized
00:02:50 - Liam O'Connor: can you share recommended instance types and expected latencies for the quantized 13B model?

00:02:58 - Marcus Patel: rough numbers: on gpus comparable to a4 or t4 family, 13B quantized might be 80-120ms p50 for short prompts with batching disabled; p95 can go to 300-500ms depending on seq length. those numbers are optimistic and we'll run bench on your staging to confirm
00:03:18 - Noah Kim: that p95 range is higher than we expected, how does batching impact throughput vs latency for customer-facing endpoints?

00:03:26 - Marcus Patel: batching improves throughput and reduces per-token cost, but increases tail latency depending on batch window. Redwood Optimize suggests adaptive batching and prefix caching to balance latency SLOs — we'll include config examples
00:03:40 - Sofia Martinez: for marketplace listing we usually show 'typical latency' and 'cost per 1k tokens' fields — do you have unit economics we can publish?

00:03:48 - Ava Chen: we can provide a range, but we prefer customers run a quick baseline on their workload. we'll provide a cost guideline: best-effort numbers for hosted vs dedicated vs private with quantization levels

00:03:58 - Liam O'Connor: security questions — our SSO and compliance team will want SOC2 type 2, audit logs, and KMS integration. how does redwood support customer-managed keys in private deployments?

00:04:08 - Marcus Patel: private supports KMS/HSM via customer-managed keys; control plane can be optional or isolated. audit logs are shipped to customer log sinks, and we can provide an audit schema for the listing. we'll also share our SOC attestation docs as part of the vendor pack
00:04:22 - Noah Kim: perfect. on networking: we need steps for VPC peering, allowed ports, and egress rules. do you have a minimal ports list?

00:04:30 - Marcus Patel: yes — primarily gRPC/HTTP ports for inference, health checks, and monitoring. we'll include a one-page networking checklist. some environments require egress lock-down so we also document an air-gapped on-prem variant with manifest files

00:04:46 - Sofia Martinez: about the validation pipeline — we run automatic integration tests after listing submission. we need a test harness or smoke tests to validate the integration. can your SEs provide a test endpoint and sample payloads?
00:04:58 - Priya Rao: we can provide a staging endpoint and sample prompts; recommend we define 5 smoke tests: auth, simple generation, streaming, embedding, model switch fallback
00:05:08 - Liam O'Connor: great. timeline—we're aiming for a soft-launch in early august. what's realistic for you to complete artifacts and tests?
00:05:16 - Ava Chen: if we start immediately, we can share listing assets by 6/18, SE bench by 6/25, and a joint validation week late july. that aligns with an early-aug soft-launch
00:05:28 - Noah Kim: do you have a recommended QA checklist for marketplace certification? sometimes the marketplace requires specific logging formats and performance baselines
00:05:36 - Marcus Patel: we'll map requirements to your checklist — items like response schema conformity, rate limiting headers, and error codes — we'll produce a compatibility matrix

00:05:46 - Sofia Martinez: one more practical ask — thumbnails and a short promo video are required for highlighted listings. do you have an existing one or should we plan a joint customer-facing video?
00:05:56 - Ava Chen: we have a short product overview video; for marketplace highlight we can co-brand a 30s clip if marketing teams coordinate. priya can lead that
00:06:06 - Priya Rao: yes happy to coordinate, i'll follow up with asset specs and marketing contacts
00:06:12 - Liam O'Connor: switching back to reference arch specifics — the private deploy example: do you support both helm and operator-based installs?

00:06:20 - Marcus Patel: primary distributions: helm chart for our runtime and a lightweight operator for lifecycle in air-gapped setups. operator helps with upgrades and kv cache migration between nodes
00:06:34 - Noah Kim: any known gotchas for GPU scheduling? our infra team uses custom node labels for shared clusters

00:06:40 - Marcus Patel: we recommend dedicated node pools for inference with GPU isolation. we can provide tolerations and nodeSelector examples; note that the runtime needs persistent kv cache on fast nvme for warm-starts
00:06:54 - Sofia Martinez: for the listing's technical fields we need sample API responses. can you paste one?
00:07:00 - Marcus Patel: sure — sample: {status: 200, choices: [{text: "..."}], usage: {tokens: 128}} — apologies if transcription catches brackets weirdly but we'll provide JSON files
00:07:14 - Liam O'Connor: perf benchmarks — would you run a quick baseline on our staging region (eu-west-1) once we handover creds?
00:07:22 - Marcus Patel: yes, please share staging creds through our secure onboarding flow. we prefer temporary credentials and will rotate keys after testing
00:07:30 - Noah Kim: regarding fallback policies — can redwood route to a smaller model to keep latency under an SLO if capacity constrained?

00:07:38 - Marcus Patel: yes — smart routing and model variants are supported. we can show how to configure a policy: e.g., route to quantized 7B if 13B CPU/GPU pool is saturated. will include example policy in docs
00:07:50 - Sofia Martinez: licensing & pricing: marketplace requires a price band and an MSRP. do you have a recommended structure for hosted vs dedicated vs private?

00:07:58 - Ava Chen: we'll propose a tiered model: hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated committed capacity (monthly), private licensing + support fee. we'll outline suggested MSRP ranges but final pricing typically negotiated
00:08:10 - Liam O'Connor: legal onboarding — our procurement will request vendor-signed data processing addendum and standard security questionnaire. can you route legal contact?
00:08:18 - Ava Chen: yes i'll introduce our legal and security contacts after the call. we'll also attach SOC2 and ISO attestations
00:08:26 - Noah Kim: two technical clarifications: how do you handle model updates/rollouts in private deployments without downtime?

00:08:34 - Marcus Patel: can do canary rollouts with KV cache compatibility checks. images are versioned and we support a canary pool; if cache incompatibility detected we fall back to cold start then warm caches in background
00:08:46 - Priya Rao: we'll include a one-pager on rollouts in the reference arch doc
00:08:54 - Sofia Martinez: regarding observability — marketplace needs a basic integration for metrics — prometheus endpoints or push gateway?

00:09:02 - Marcus Patel: we emit prometheus metrics and can push to a customer's gateway; traces are compatible with opentelemetry. we'll attach sample metrics naming and a small dashboard JSON for import
00:09:14 - Liam O'Connor: great. any blockers right now from redwood side?
00:09:18 - Ava Chen: main blockers are staging credentials and marketing assets. once those are shared we'll proceed with bench and listing draft
00:09:26 - Noah Kim: sound good. one more question — do you support marketplace-managed billing or should customers bill directly to redwood?
00:09:34 - Ava Chen: both models possible; some marketplaces prefer centralized billing through platform. we'll provide recommended options and contract language for each

00:09:44 - Sofia Martinez: ok, let's capture the required artifacts list so my team can validate: listing copy, screenshots, sample API responses, terraform snippet, smoke tests, metrics dashboard, security docs, marketing assets
00:09:56 - Marcus Patel: adding perf report and deployment manifest to that list

00:10:02 - Liam O'Connor: and push a low-friction onboarding path for early customers
ash maybe a quick-start template and a test credit code
00:10:10 - Priya Rao: we've done promo credits before; we'll coordinate with partner ops and see what we can offer for launch
00:10:18 - Ava Chen: ok, let's quickly recap action items and owners...

00:10:22 - Ava Chen: Ava will share listing template and logos, Marcus will run bench and provide ref arch snippets, Priya will lead marketing coordination, Sofia will provide staging VPC, Noah compiles on-prem notes
00:10:36 - Liam O'Connor: thanks all. we'll plan to review the listing draft week of 6/22 and run validation in july. any final q's?
00:10:46 - Noah Kim: none from me, thanks
00:10:48 - Sofia Martinez: thanks everyone, i'll watch for the template
00:10:52 - Ava Chen: thanks team — we'll follow up in writing with the assets and calendar invites for the validation week, bye
00:11:00 - [call ended]
